claims.text: A controlled aging heat treatment can produce uniformly distributed, coherent nanoscale precipitates in the target aerospace-fastener HEA.
The aging-induced precipitates will enhance mechanical durability.
The aging treatment will improve room-temperature creep resistance.
The aging treatment will increase corrosion resistance.
The as-cast or solution-treated initial material has a homogeneous microstructure without an optimized precipitate distribution.
Aging below the gamma-prime solvus will retain a desirable matrix phase and ensure precipitate coherence.
The structural mediator is a uniform distribution of coherent nanoscale precipitates, such as L12-type precipitates, within the matrix.
The precipitates stabilize the microstructure.
The precipitates obstruct dislocation motion and thereby increase strength and durability.
The precipitates improve creep resistance by impeding time-dependent deformation mechanisms.
The precipitates improve corrosion resistance by reducing the active area for corrosive attack and stabilizing the microstructure.
Relative to the untreated baseline, aged material will exhibit higher hardness and tensile strength.
Relative to the untreated baseline, aged material will exhibit a lower room-temperature creep rate.
Relative to the untreated baseline, aged material will exhibit a lower electrochemical corrosion rate.
The predicted improvements will hold at ambient service temperatures and under typical aerospace environmental exposures.
Failure to meet optimal aging parameters may limit the treatment's effectiveness.
Compositional variation can alter precipitate formation and the optimal aging temperature and duration.
Precipitate morphology creates uncertainty in the magnitude of the corrosion-resistance improvement.
The experiment compares aged specimens with untreated or solely solution-treated controls under identical mechanical, creep, and electrochemical test conditions.

The hypothesis is falsified if treated specimens show no statistically significant improvement beyond experimental error in hardness, tensile strength, creep rate, and corrosion rate relative to controls.
